key_big: SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS prove two triangles congruent
body_html:
How it works

Congruent figures — ‘geometric twins’ — have the same shape and size; one fits exactly on the other.

Two triangles are congruent if they match by SSS (three sides), SAS (two sides and the angle between them), ASA (two angles and the side between) or RHS (right angle, hypotenuse, side).

Write the vertices in matching order: △ABC ≅ △PQR means A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R, so AB = PQ and ∠C = ∠R.

Example

AB = PQ, BC = QR, CA = RP. Are △ABC and △PQR congruent?

Three pairs of equal sides

Answer: Yes, by SSS

Example

△LMN ≅ △XYZ. Which side equals MN?

M ↔ Y, N ↔ Z

Answer: YZ

Common mistakes

  • Thinking three equal angles (AAA) make triangles congruent.
  • Using SAS when the angle is not between the two sides.
  • Matching the vertices in the wrong order.

items.q: Given △MQF ≅ △WTJ, complete the statement: △FMQ ≅ ?
items.e: Keep each pair of matching vertices together: F ↔ J, M ↔ W, Q ↔ T. So △FMQ ≅ △JWT.

items.q: Given △VTF ≅ △WZX, which segment is congruent to FT?
items.e: Match the letters in order: F → X and T → Z. So FT ≅ XZ.

items.q: Given △EQN ≅ △SYA, which angle is congruent to ∠N?
items.e: N is in the same position as A in the statement, so ∠N ≅ ∠A.

items.q: Given △JXY ≅ △KRB, which segment is congruent to XY?
items.e: Match the letters in order: X → R and Y → B. So XY ≅ RB.

items.q: Given △DUM ≅ △SKA, which segment is congruent to DM?
items.e: Match the letters in order: D → S and M → A. So DM ≅ SA.

items.q: Given △QVN ≅ △TPU, which angle is congruent to ∠Q?
items.e: Q is in the same position as T in the statement, so ∠Q ≅ ∠T.

items.q: Given △YZR ≅ △JLC, which angle is congruent to ∠Z?
items.e: Z is in the same position as L in the statement, so ∠Z ≅ ∠L.

items.q: Given △DBM ≅ △KUN, which angle is congruent to ∠M?
items.e: M is in the same position as N in the statement, so ∠M ≅ ∠N.

items.q: Given △NEM ≅ △AHS, which angle is congruent to ∠E?
items.e: E is in the same position as H in the statement, so ∠E ≅ ∠H.

items.q: Given △FVJ ≅ △YKZ, which angle is congruent to ∠J?
items.e: J is in the same position as Z in the statement, so ∠J ≅ ∠Z.

items.q: Given △FGN ≅ △YUT, which angle is congruent to ∠G?
items.e: G is in the same position as U in the statement, so ∠G ≅ ∠U.

items.q: Given △WXR ≅ △SBN, which segment is congruent to RX?
items.e: Match the letters in order: R → N and X → B. So RX ≅ NB.

items.q: Given △NSZ ≅ △GJC, complete the statement: △NZS ≅ ?
items.e: Keep each pair of matching vertices together: N ↔ G, Z ↔ C, S ↔ J. So △NZS ≅ △GCJ.

items.q: Given △DVQ ≅ △UYH, which angle is congruent to ∠D?
items.e: D is in the same position as U in the statement, so ∠D ≅ ∠U.

items.q: Given △RKX ≅ △HEW, which segment is congruent to KX?
items.e: Match the letters in order: K → E and X → W. So KX ≅ EW.

items.q: Given △QKJ ≅ △YUS, which segment is congruent to JK?
items.e: Match the letters in order: J → S and K → U. So JK ≅ SU.

items.q: Given △FVK ≅ △JSY, which angle is congruent to ∠K?
items.e: K is in the same position as Y in the statement, so ∠K ≅ ∠Y.

items.q: Given △XSN ≅ △RMA, which segment is congruent to NS?
items.e: Match the letters in order: N → A and S → M. So NS ≅ AM.

items.q: Given △YCU ≅ △RSX, which angle is congruent to ∠U?
items.e: U is in the same position as X in the statement, so ∠U ≅ ∠X.

items.q: Given △QKP ≅ △AYB, which angle is congruent to ∠P?
items.e: P is in the same position as B in the statement, so ∠P ≅ ∠B.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, ∠G ≅ ∠L and ∠H ≅ ∠M. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as HI: HI ≅ MN.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠R ≅ ∠U and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as ST: ST ≅ VW.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠J ≅ ∠M and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as KL: KL ≅ NO.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, AB ≅ DE and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠B is between AB and BC: BC ≅ EF.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, PQ ≅ XY and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠Q is between PQ and QR: QR ≅ YZ.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠P ≅ ∠X and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as QR: QR ≅ YZ.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠P ≅ ∠X and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. PQ is between ∠P and ∠Q: PQ ≅ XY.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, ∠I and ∠N are right angles, and GH ≅ LM (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. GI and LN are legs: GI ≅ LN.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠T and ∠W are right angles, and RS ≅ UV (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. RT and UW are legs: RT ≅ UW.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, AB ≅ DE and BC ≅ EF. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: AC ≅ DF.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠L and ∠O are right angles, and JK ≅ MN (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. JL and MO are legs: JL ≅ MO.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, RS ≅ UV and ST ≅ VW. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: RT ≅ UW.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as BC: BC ≅ EF.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, ∠G ≅ ∠L and ∠H ≅ ∠M. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. GH is between ∠G and ∠H: GH ≅ LM.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, GH ≅ LM and ∠H ≅ ∠M. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠H is between GH and HI: HI ≅ MN.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, RS ≅ UV and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠S is between RS and ST: ST ≅ VW.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠C and ∠F are right angles, and AB ≅ DE (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by RHS?
items.e: RHS needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. AC and DF are legs: AC ≅ DF.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠J ≅ ∠M and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. JK is between ∠J and ∠K: JK ≅ MN.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. AB is between ∠A and ∠B: AB ≅ DE.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, PQ ≅ XY and QR ≅ YZ. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: PR ≅ XZ.

items.q: △GHK ≅ △LMN. HK = 2x − 11 and MN = 13. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCT): HK = MN, so 2x − 11 = 13 and x = 12.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. RT = 2x + 23 and UW = 37. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCT): RT = UW, so 2x + 23 = 37 and x = 7.

items.q: △PQR ≅ △XYZ. QP = 7x + 8 and YX = 22. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCT): QP = YX, so 7x + 8 = 22 and x = 2.

items.q: △GHK ≅ △LMN. KH = 7x + 5 and NM = 5x + 15. Find NM.

items.e: ∠N corresponds to ∠K, so ∠K = 180 − 52 − 70 = 58. Then 4x + 6 = 58, so x = 13.

items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCT): KL = NP, so 4x − 12 = 24 and x = 9.

△JKL ≅ △MNP. KL = 3x + 17 and NP = 38. Find x.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. RS = 3x and UV = 4x − 10. Find UV.

items.e: ∠Y corresponds to ∠Q, so ∠Q = 180 − 69 − 49 = 62. Then 6x − 22 = 62, so x = 14.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. LK = 3x − 19 and PN = 2x − 9. Find PN.

items.e: ∠E corresponds to ∠B, so ∠B = 180 − 41 − 56 = 83. Then 5x + 33 = 83, so x = 10.
